| `changelog-check` fails with "Failed to get changed files" | Checkout step is missing `fetch-depth: 0`; ensure `changelog-check.yml` has `fetch-depth: 0` on the `actions/checkout` step |
| `validate-issue` never starts after issue open/edit | Missing `issues: write` permission on `GITHUB_TOKEN`; workflow file syntax error; branch protection blocking Actions |
| Issue stays unlabelled after validation run | LLM API key missing or invalid; `manage_labels.mjs` failed to create labels (check for 403/404 in logs) |
| `ready-for-dev` applied but `code-generation` never triggers | Workflow trigger mismatch (label name drift vs `config/labels.yaml`); `AI_PR_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` lacks `contents: write` |
| Generation run completes but no PR is created | Empty LLM output (no valid JSON patch); the patch was rejected by a guardrail (`rejected=true`; see the "Code Generation: Patch Rejected" row); the issue was blocked (`blocked=true`; see the "Code Generation: Blocked" row); `AI_PR_TOKEN` scope too narrow; **Allow GitHub Actions to create pull requests** disabled |
| PR opens but files are wrong or empty | Prompt template issue (`generation-user.md` placeholders not resolved); model returned malformed JSON; `output_writer.mjs` rejected paths (absolute, `..` traversal, or a protected path — `.github/`, `scripts/`, `config/`, `prompts/`, `checkpoints/`, `metrics/`, `observability/`, `docs/`, `README.md`, `package.json`, lock files, `.npmrc`/`.yarnrc*`; see ADR-0021), or a rewrite that would cut an existing file of 20+ lines by more than half (`would shrink from N to M lines`, also raised when more than half of the non-whitespace content goes). Both stages escalate instead of failing (ADR-0019): generation posts `Code Generation: Patch Rejected` on the issue, applies `needs-human` and opens no PR (`code_gen.skipped` / `pr_prepare.skipped`, `codegen_skip` metric); auto-fix: `reason: "guardrail_rejected"`, below. A documentation-only issue always ends here: edit `README.md`/`docs/` by hand |
| Issue loses `ready-for-dev`, gets `needs-human` and a "Code Generation: Blocked" comment, no PR | Generation could not implement the issue (ADR-0029 amendment; `code_gen.skipped` with `reason: "blocked"`, `codegen_skip` metric, `blocked=true`). The comment names the source: `denylist` — every file the issue names is protected (`scripts/`, `config/`, `package.json`, …) or above 8,000 chars; implement by hand, or name a writable file if the issue was mis-scoped. `model` — the model returned `blocked: true` (typically "blocked by an unmerged PR"); merge the dependency first. `notes_only` — a `bug`/`feature` issue got only new Markdown notes; check whether the target is protected, otherwise make the issue name the code file. The planned fix in the comment is the model's proposal, not a written change. Then remove `needs-human` and re-apply `ready-for-dev`. `code_gen.error` with `reason: "blocked"`: the escalation itself failed (GitHub API); the labels may be half-applied, fix them by hand |
| Issue gets `needs-human` and a "Code Generation: Patch Rejected" comment, no PR | The generated patch broke a guardrail (ADR-0019); the comment lists `rules` and the reason per file. `module_system`: `require(` in an `.mjs` file or a CommonJS file turned ESM. `exported_signature`: an exported function removed or reshaped — for an intended signature change, name the function in the issue body; a removal is never unlocked and is done by hand. `unresolved_import`: an import that is neither a builtin, an existing relative file, nor a `package.json` dependency — declare the package by hand first, or ask for the built-in. `unshown_file` / `withheld_file`: the model edited a file the issue did not name, or one above 8,000 chars — name the file, or split it. `mass_deletion` / `test_count_drop` / `destructive_shrink`: the model rewrote instead of editing. Then remove `needs-human` and re-apply `ready-for-dev` |
| `pr-review` never posts a comment | No open PR found for the push branch (exits silently by design); LLM API error; `pull-requests: write` permission missing |
| `pr-review` run succeeds in seconds without a new comment or review (log: `Skipping review`, event `review.skipped`) | Expected (ADR-0028): `already_reviewed` — the newest trusted review comment's `<!-- adl-review sha=… -->` marker already names the PR head with `APPROVE`/`REQUEST_CHANGES` (the `push` and `pull_request: opened` runs of a new PR; `WITHHELD` never dedups; comments by non-members are ignored); `superseded` — the PR head moved past the run's commit, and the newer push's run reviews it. Use **Re-run jobs** to force a review of the same head |
| An LLM step is slow, log shows `retry` with `waitMs: 60000` and Groq 429 or 413 `rate_limit_exceeded` | Expected (ADR-0028 amendment): the 8K TPM is shared by every PR and stage of the org, so a run queues behind the others. A 429, or a 413 whose body has `"code":"rate_limit_exceeded"`, is retried; without a `try again in Xs` / `Retry-After` hint it waits one full TPM window (60 s). Each LLM step allows `GROQ_MAX_RETRIES` such waits (review and validation 12, auto-fix and generation 15, evals 20) inside its job `timeout-minutes` (15 / 15 / 20 / 20 / 120). Nothing to do |
